newsitem.title: JAPAN: Creator of Japan's Godzilla films dead at 86.
newsitem.headline: Creator of Japan's Godzilla films dead at 86.

text.p: Tomoyuki Tanaka, the father of the Godzilla monster movie series, died of a stroke at 86 on Wednesday, 16 months after his giant lizard-like creation was killed off in the final Japanese episode, his family said.

Tanaka, 86, a former chairman of the Toho Co. film production firm, rose to fame in 1954 with the film "Godzilla", the story of a lizard-like creature awakened from a long slumber by hydrogen bomb testing in the South Pacific.
Godzilla caught on in Japan and gained cult status abroad, where some read the film as an allegory on the perils of the atomic age.
Tanaka produced 22 Godzilla films before the much-loved lizard met his match at the claws of an equally bizarre creation in the December 1995 "Godzilla versus Destroyer".
In "Godzilla versus Destroyer", which drew crowds only normally seen for popular Hollywood hits, Godzilla first ravages Hong Kong, turning the city into a fiery blaze.

Godzilla then returned to Tokyo for a final battle royal with The Destroyer, a monster created from oceanic microbes which melded together after the "oxygen destroyer" sent Godzilla away with his tail between his legs in the first film.
Tanaka's rampaging, reptilian brainchild will outlive his creator, however, reappearing in a 1998 film by the director of the hit U.S. movie "Independence Day", film maker Toho Co. said last October.

Hollywood director and life-long Godzilla fan Roland Emmerich will continue the tradition that Tanaka, a former chairman of Toho, began in 1954 with the black-and-white film "Godzilla", the firm said.
The name of the monster, which always made comebacks after repeatedly perishing in movies, is a cross between "god" and a Japanese word for whale, "kujira".

Tanaka, who joined Toho after graduating from university in 1940, went on to produce more than 200 films, including "Akahige" (Red Beard) and "Kagemusha" with Academy Award-winning director Akira Kurosawa.
